reasoning: Re-arm the Schneider -15% rail at €229.08 (€269.50 entry x 0.85) sized at 4 of 5 shares, not 5. Pre-drawn cap trim on Schneider at €310. Today's +10.8% gap took the sleeve to 14.3% of book without a purchase; at €310 it is ~15.4%, a real breach of my hard limit, and the same share is a +15% gain on my €269.50 entry. One order does the risk work and books the profit — same technique as the LVMH €560 and Danone €76 lines.

Harvest the two-day gap: $390.54 to $464.72 on 110M then 56M shares is a gift on the position that was my deepest red seven sessions ago. One of three shares locks +10.6% and takes cash from 7.5% to ~11% — dry powder I earned rather than raised in a panic. Two shares keep compounding.

Re-author the floor at the correct size after the trim: with two shares left, a one-share stop reduces instead of deletes. Level moves from the stale -15%-from-entry $357.22 up to the $420.26 cost basis — a winner this violent is not permitted to round-trip back into a loss.

AAPL carried a $340 upside gate and nothing underneath it — a naked downside on a name that just fell 7.4% on record volume. The -15%-from-entry floor sits at $223.89, which is meaningless at +17%, so the gate goes at $290, under Friday's break, on 1 of 2 shares.

Société Générale closed 07/30 at €81.10, +5.71% on 3.30M shares (~2.0x the 60-day average), a new 52-week-high close with the €82.15 high setting the 52-week high itself — the first genuine volume thrust out of the EU bank complex, which has been making highs on sub-1x volume for weeks. 3m RS +23.4%, 6m +245.8%, best in the sector. Buy-stop at €82.30 so it only fires on continuation above the 52-week high, never on my chasing a stale print. 29 shares is 23.8% NAV at the trigger and stays inside the 25% cap even on a €86 gap-through fill.

Schneider gapped €256.80 → €270.25 on 07/30 and ran to a €286.10 high, closing €284.60 at the top of the range, +10.83% on 1.54M vs ~920k average (1.67x) — the single biggest one-day thrust in the STOXX 600 and it reclaims six weeks of chop in one candle, back to 96.9% of the €293.70 52-week high. It's a reversal thrust, not an established trend, so it has to prove itself: buy-stop at €287.00 clears the whole day's range. 8 shares is 22.9% NAV at the trigger, inside the cap even on a €310 gap-through.

Cut the broken follow-through and fund the best chart in the index. MMM peaked $184.90 on 7/28 and has closed lower four straight sessions to $176.28, below my $178.23 entry and 4.7% off its high, while the leaders made new highs — it is the only name I own that stopped advancing. Volume is drying up (1.87M vs 3.56M avg) so it isn't collapsing, but I don't pay 17.5% of book to wait for a name to decide. No averaging down, no hoping.

The cleanest thrust on the board and the reason SPY reclaimed $744: 7/30 gapped $390.54 to open $437.90 and closed $451.10 on 110.16M vs ~28M avg (3.9x), then 7/31 followed through to a fresh 52-week high $464.72, closing at 0.996 of the day's high $466.84 on 56.47M (2.0x) with a low of $449.55 — the gap was never tested. RS 1.10 vs SPY over 3 months (+14.0% vs +3.9%). Two-day thrusts that hold their gap on declining-but-still-heavy volume are the setups that pay 40%. 5 shares at ~$464.72 = ~$2,324, 19.3% of book, inside my 25% cap, funded by the MMM sale.

Stop armed at entry, no exceptions. $444 sits under the 7/31 follow-through low $449.55 and wide of the obvious $449 line — equity triggers settle on the close and a gap eats thin stops, which is exactly how NVDA filled at $196.51. The entire thesis is that the earnings gap holds; a close at $444 means it is filling and I am wrong fast. -4.5% risk, well inside my -10% rule.

Ratchet $116.50 to $119. PRU has held every day since the breakout — lowest post-breakout low is $120.67, and 7/31 closed $122.08 above my $121.89 entry — so there is no reason to leave $5.50 of air under it. $119 is wide of the obvious $119.96 (the 7/24 pre-breakout close) and under the whole post-breakout range; a close there puts price back inside the $114-119 base and voids the move. Cuts my risk from -4.4% to -2.4% from entry.

Second weakness rung, priced to the tape at €28.90 — just under the €29.26 low of the last 32 sessions, so it only fires on a genuine shelf break rather than on noise. The strong euro is a structural headwind for CAC exporters and 07-30 broke down on 2.4x volume; if €29.26 goes, the 2x CAC thesis is finished and I want to be out of the second half without waiting for a session. Still locks +€2.76/share on my €26.145 blend — a gain, not a loss. Mirrors the €31.50 upside rung exactly: 20 up, 20 down, 40 held, no orphan and no over-commitment.

Rebuy the shares my own stop took, but only on proof. 7/31 closed 200.75 — above the 191-192 base I said was dead, above both prior closes, on 139M shares. $207 reclaims the 7/23-7/24 shelf (208.76, 206.84) and makes the 7/27-7/29 breakdown a two-day bull trap rather than a trend. Takes NVDA 6 to 12 (~22% of NAV, inside my cap) for ~$1,242. If it stalls under 207 I never pay, and I keep the powder for RTX/NOC.

Manufacture powder from the sleeve with a four-month dead ratio. ETH/BTC 0.02966 has not moved since April; the rotation I bought this for never came, and my only good ETH trade was trimming into strength at €1,923. Stacks beneath the existing 0.25@€2,400 rung so the whole sleeve exits in two stages on bounces rather than getting dumped at €1,628. Below the €1,995 basis (~€49 realized loss, no PFU on a loss) but €449 of live powder at the moment BTC retests a twice-tested cycle floor beats a dead beta bet.

Bottom peel rung re-armed at €68k with the clock moved to 2027-01-31. Same level, same size — only the date changes. From €54,900 a +24% move by 09-15 was a coin flip on a broken box; past the rotation it is simply the first stage of the euphoria ladder. Gross ~€328 over the €59,807 basis clears 26bps taker plus PFU 30% with room.

Middle peel rung re-armed at €75k, clock aligned to 2027-01-31. €75k by mid-September from €54,900 was a 37% ask in six weeks — a rung that expires before markup arrives is a rung I never had. Gross ~€608 over the €59,807 basis, +25% before fees.

Top peel rung re-armed at €85k, clock aligned to 2027-01-31, keeping the €68k/€75k/€85k three-stage ladder intact on one consistent horizon. Gross ~€1,008 over the €59,807 basis, +42% before fees. Leaves the 0.015 tail unmanaged by design — the winners are the ones you don't sell early.

Stage the dollar-short as a buy-stop at 1.1560, above Friday's 1.1550 high and above every print in the July 1.1355-1.1438 range, so it buys resolution of the breakdown rather than my opinion of it. I pick EURUSD over AUDUSD/NZDUSD deliberately: those rallied harder but carry the yen-repatriation beta that just cost me the EURJPY leg, while EURUSD is a clean Fed-dovish-vs-ECB-on-hold trade in the deepest book on the board. Sized at ~13% of a ~EUR 10.0k book, not 20%, because I already run EUR-long through EURGBP and I will not pretend two euro legs are two ideas. Rail follows the fill next session.

Re-open Brent only on the base resolving up — above 15.40 clears the July 23 high of 15.37 and the whole post-flush range from the 13.87 low. Copper and platinum at new highs say industrial demand is not dying, so the July crude flush was supply and positioning, not the economy. ~EUR 1,170, ~14% NAV, and it clears cash even if the pending PHAG add fires first.

Hard -12% rail on the Brent tranche the moment it can exist, from the 15.40 entry. 13.55 sits below the July 28 flush low of 13.87, so it is a disaster stop and not a range-low stop — the mistake I made cutting this sleeve at 13.50 in June. Rejects harmlessly on position if the buy never fires.

Exit the full Apple line at market after a -7.4% gap from 333.43 to 308.91 on 127m shares, 2.5x normal, straight through every shelf since June; the chart that justified holding is gone and my $340 take-profit is now ten percent out of reach, so I bank +17% on the $263.40 cost rather than manage a broken position. FX stance: the asset leg and the currency leg have turned negative together — DXY 99.80 and EURUSD 1.1527 mean a falling US asset is now also a shrinking euro asset, and I would rather realise the translation while it is still worth something.

Exit healthcare at market four sessions after entry: XLV fell from 167.26 to 162.55 while SPY rose 0.83% to a new high, destroying 3.6% of relative strength — and relative strength as defensive leadership was the entire thesis, exactly the way XLU's was falsified before its rail ever fired. In EUR the line is -4.1%, not -0.5%. FX stance: this closes my last discretionary dollar equity beyond NVDA and takes the USD sleeve from 24% to 5% on the week the dollar broke 100 — I am not paying a 1.4% translation tax to hold a lagging sector.

BNP closed 108.84 at a fresh 60-day high on an outside-up day, the top of a sector where GLE +5.7%, INGA +5.1%, ABN +4.1% and every major European bank sits at its 60-day high — a broad bid, not a single-stock gap, which is what I want after Airbus. The driver is the same one moving my macro: JGB/term-premium repricing steepening curves globally, and bank NIM is the cleanest long-only expression of it. Sized at 13 shares, 14% of book, inside my 20% cap. FX stance: deliberately EUR-native and currency-neutral — a bank earns in the currency I report in, so unlike Airbus or luxury there is no strong-euro headwind hiding in the earnings; this is an asset bet with the FX leg switched off on purpose.

Protective stop on the new bank line at 104.00, beneath the 105.12 low of the breakout day and above the 103.46 pivot of 07-23 — about -4.5% from entry, the leash a grind deserves versus the tighter one a gap gets. If the yen carry unwind finally reaches equities, banks are where it lands first and I leave without arguing. FX stance: EUR in, EUR out, no currency leg.

Re-armed Airbus stop, raised from 199.00 to 202.00 — my journal said 'gap fills, I leave,' and the gap floor is 202.50, so a rail 1.7% below it was slack, not discipline. Price has faded 212.00 to 204.00 on rising volume and now sits 0.7% above that floor; this cuts risk from -4.7% to -3.3% of entry without pre-empting a chart that has not yet broken. FX stance: EUR-native containment, though I note Airbus is a USD-revenue, EUR-cost exporter — a euro heading for 1.170 is a slow headwind in the earnings, one more reason the leash shortens rather than lengthens.

Re-armed gold breakout add above €118.00, cut from two shares to one purely for cap headroom: at 15 shares the sleeve is already 17% of book, and two shares filling at 118-120 would print 19.7-20.2% and risk a MAX_POSITION rejection at fire time. One share keeps the confirmation trade alive at a safe 18.6%. The €112 stop stays exactly where it has sat since April. FX stance: EUR-native metal — and I note gold fell 1.5% on Friday as the dollar broke, so euro-gold is the muted version of the debasement trade; it only gets more of my euros if it clears the €117.19 July high on its own merit.
